# NREL 2011 cellulosic ethanol plant, Area 500: product, solids and water recovery (distillation, dehydration, separation)

Source: Humbird et al., NREL/TP-5100-47764 (May 2011), report pp. 44-46 (section 3.5) and Appendix A/E. The plant processes 2,205 dry US tons/day (2,000 dry tonnes/day) of corn stover. This area is one part of the plant; its inputs come from other areas at the flows below, and its outputs go to other areas.

## Compounds (DWSIM stand-ins)

DWSIM's databank has no biomass polymers or lumped solids, so the report's components are represented by these compounds (by mass):

- Ethanol, Water, CO2, O2, N2, Ammonia, Methane, Acetic acid: themselves
- Furfurals (furfural + HMF): Acetic acid (furfural-water is partly immiscible; its liquid-liquid split stalls the column solver)
- Other Organics (glycerol, succinic acid, ...): Glycerol
- Glucose: Tetraethylene glycol
- Xylose: Triethylene glycol
- Cellulose: PentaEthylene Glycol
- Xylan: TetraPropylene Glycol
- Soluble solids lumps: other sugars, sugar oligomers, organic and inorganic soluble solids, sulfuric acid: HexaEthylene Glycol
- Insoluble solids lumps: lignin, protein, cell mass, acetate, other structural carbohydrates, other insolubles: HexaPropylene Glycol

Every stand-in carries the report component's MASS (1 kg of glucose is 1 kg of Tetraethylene glycol). The glycols are non-volatile and water-miscible, like the sugars and solids they replace (DWSIM's own sugar compounds stall its rigorous column solver). A reaction on a stand-in keeps its mass balance by scaling the coefficients with molar mass, e.g. glucose -> 2 ethanol + 2 CO2 becomes 1 Tetraethylene glycol -> 2.1562 Ethanol + 2.1562 Carbon dioxide. Missing NRTL pairs are treated as ideal.

Use these DWSIM compound names (only those present in the area's streams are needed): Acetic acid, Ammonia, Carbon dioxide, Ethanol, Glycerol, HexaEthylene Glycol, HexaPropylene Glycol, Nitrogen, Oxygen, PentaEthylene Glycol, TetraPropylene Glycol, Tetraethylene glycol, Triethylene glycol, Water. Use the NRTL property package (ethanol-water). Stream ids are the report's stream numbers prefixed with S (e.g. S501).

### Design basis (report section 3.5.2, design basis text)

- Beer from fermentation (5.4 wt % ethanol) is fed to the beer column D-501 after an economizing exchanger H-512 against the beer column bottoms. The bottoms are cooled to 47 C in that economizer (a suitable temperature for liquid-solid separation).
- D-501 removes the CO2 and as little ethanol as possible to the overhead while removing about 90 % of the water to the bottoms. The ethanol leaves as a vapour side draw and is fed directly to the rectification column D-502. Both columns are modelled in the report with rigorous VLE (Aspen RADFRAC).
- D-501: 32 stages at 48 % efficiency; feed on the fourth tray from the top; molar reflux ratio 3:1; overhead vented to the scrubber (about 85 % CO2, 11 % ethanol and close to 4 % water); all of the CO2 and only 0.3 % of the feed ethanol go overhead; about 0.8 % of the feed ethanol is lost in the bottoms; more than 99 % of the feed ethanol leaves as the vapour side draw at tray 8, at 40 wt % ethanol. Overhead pressure 2 atm (15 psig). Reboiler H-501 uses low-pressure steam at 9.5 atm (125 psig).
- D-502: 45 stages at 76 % efficiency; the D-501 vapour enters on tray 33 counting from the top; the molecular-sieve recycle (72 wt % ethanol) enters on tray 14; molar reflux ratio 3.5:1 to obtain an overhead vapour of 92.5 % w/w ethanol and bottoms of 0.05 % w/w ethanol. The overhead leaves as saturated vapour at about 1.6 atm (PFD-P120-A502/A503 operating pressure). The bottoms are recycled to pretreatment as dilution water.
- Vent scrubber T-512: the beer column overhead and the seed and production fermentor vents are scrubbed with water; it recovers 99 % of the vented ethanol; the effluent (about 1.8 wt % ethanol) returns to the beer well.
- Molecular sieve M-503: the saturated D-502 overhead vapour is superheated and fed to one of two adsorption columns, which removes 95 % of the water and a small amount of ethanol; the 99.5 % ethanol vapour is cooled against the regeneration condensate and finally condensed with cooling water and pumped to storage. Regeneration: a slipstream of pure ethanol vapour strips the water off under vacuum; the mixture (about 70-72 wt % ethanol) is condensed and returned to D-502.
- Pressure filter S-505: operated without a wash; the cake is dried with air to 35 % moisture; the drying air goes to the combustor and the pressed stillage water to wastewater treatment.

### Modelling notes (solver limits found by PlantAgent's engine tests on this case, not from the report)

- DWSIM's rigorous column does not converge with CO2 or O2 in it: take the dissolved CO2 off the preheated beer ahead of D-501 (flash or component_separator) and send it with the D-501 vent to T-512.
- D-501's vapour side draw carries more vapour than leaves the top, which the column solver does not converge: model D-501 from the side-draw tray down, with a partial condenser whose vapour product (vapor_mol_s) is the side draw S510, and a small reflux ratio.
- D-502 with a partial condenser and almost no liquid distillate does not converge: use a total condenser and let H-503 vaporise and superheat the overhead before the sieve; report the condenser duty with that caveat.
- T-512 (absorber with CO2) and M-503 (adsorption) are fixed-split separations here (component_separator) at the documented recoveries.
- Every equipment item on the P&ID must appear as a unit with its tag.


## Equipment (Appendix A)

- H-512 Beer column feed interchanger: plate & frame; beer (cold) against beer column bottoms (hot)
- D-501 Beer column: 32 fixed-valve trays, 24 in spacing, 14 ft diameter (4.27 m), 76 ft tall; reboiler H-501 (LP steam 9.5 atm), condenser H-504
- T-512 Vent scrubber: water scrubber for the beer column and fermentation vents; inlet gas 9,681 acfm at 91 F

DWSIM's databank has no biomass polymers or lumped solids, so the report's components are represented by these compounds (by mass):

- Ethanol, Water, CO2, O2, N2, Ammonia, Methane, Acetic acid: themselves
- Furfurals (furfural + HMF): Acetic acid (furfural-water is partly immiscible; its liquid-liquid split stalls the column solver)
- Other Organics (glycerol, succinic acid, ...): Glycerol
- Glucose: Tetraethylene glycol
- Xylose: Triethylene glycol
- Cellulose: PentaEthylene Glycol
- Xylan: TetraPropylene Glycol
- Soluble solids lumps: other sugars, sugar oligomers, organic and inorganic soluble solids, sulfuric acid: HexaEthylene Glycol
- Insoluble solids lumps: lignin, protein, cell mass, acetate, other structural carbohydrates, other insolubles: HexaPropylene Glycol

Every stand-in carries the report component's MASS (1 kg of glucose is 1 kg of Tetraethylene glycol). The glycols are non-volatile and water-miscible, like the sugars and solids they replace (DWSIM's own sugar compounds stall its rigorous column solver). A reaction on a stand-in keeps its mass balance by scaling the coefficients with molar mass, e.g. glucose -> 2 ethanol + 2 CO2 becomes 1 Tetraethylene glycol -> 2.1562 Ethanol + 2.1562 Carbon dioxide. Missing NRTL pairs are treated as ideal.

Use the NRTL property package (ethanol-water). Stream ids are the report's stream numbers prefixed with S (e.g. S501).

### Design basis (report section 3.5.2, design basis text)

- Beer from fermentation (5.4 wt % ethanol) is fed to the beer column D-501 after an economizing exchanger H-512 against the beer column bottoms. The bottoms are cooled to 47 C in that economizer (a suitable temperature for liquid-solid separation).
- D-501 removes the CO2 and as little ethanol as possible to the overhead while removing about 90 % of the water to the bottoms. The ethanol leaves as a vapour side draw and is fed directly to the rectification column D-502. Both columns are modelled in the report with rigorous VLE (Aspen RADFRAC).
- D-501: 32 stages at 48 % efficiency; feed on the fourth tray from the top; molar reflux ratio 3:1; overhead vented to the scrubber (about 85 % CO2, 11 % ethanol and close to 4 % water); all of the CO2 and only 0.3 % of the feed ethanol go overhead; about 0.8 % of the feed ethanol is lost in the bottoms; more than 99 % of the feed ethanol leaves as the vapour side draw at tray 8, at 40 wt % ethanol. Overhead pressure 2 atm (15 psig). Reboiler H-501 uses low-pressure steam at 9.5 atm (125 psig).
- D-502: 45 stages at 76 % efficiency; the D-501 vapour enters on tray 33 counting from the top; the molecular-sieve recycle (72 wt % ethanol) enters on tray 14; molar reflux ratio 3.5:1 to obtain an overhead vapour of 92.5 % w/w ethanol and bottoms of 0.05 % w/w ethanol. The overhead leaves as saturated vapour at about 1.6 atm (PFD-P120-A502/A503 operating pressure). The bottoms are recycled to pretreatment as dilution water.
- Vent scrubber T-512: the beer column overhead and the seed and production fermentor vents are scrubbed with water; it recovers 99 % of the vented ethanol; the effluent (about 1.8 wt % ethanol) returns to the beer well.
- Molecular sieve M-503: the saturated D-502 overhead vapour is superheated and fed to one of two adsorption columns, which removes 95 % of the water and a small amount of ethanol; the 99.5 % ethanol vapour is cooled against the regeneration condensate and finally condensed with cooling water and pumped to storage. Regeneration: a slipstream of pure ethanol vapour strips the water off under vacuum; the mixture (about 70-72 wt % ethanol) is condensed and returned to D-502.
- Pressure filter S-505: operated without a wash; the cake is dried with air to 35 % moisture; the drying air goes to the combustor and the pressed stillage water to wastewater treatment.

### Modelling notes (solver limits found by PlantAgent's engine tests on this case, not from the report)

- DWSIM's rigorous column does not converge with CO2 or O2 in it: take the dissolved CO2 off the preheated beer ahead of D-501 (flash or component_separator) and send it with the D-501 vent to T-512.
- D-501's vapour side draw carries more vapour than leaves the top, which the column solver does not converge: model D-501 from the side-draw tray down, with a partial condenser whose vapour product (vapor_mol_s) is the side draw S510, and a small reflux ratio.
- D-502 with a partial condenser and almost no liquid distillate does not converge: use a total condenser and let H-503 vaporise and superheat the overhead before the sieve; report the condenser duty with that caveat.
- T-512 (absorber with CO2) and M-503 (adsorption) are fixed-split separations here (component_separator) at the documented recoveries.
- Every equipment item on the P&ID must appear as a unit with its tag.

args.label: trial-d501-2
assumptions: Submitted at step-limit instruction as the latest converged calibrated run; it is a partial D-501 model, not the complete Area 500 flowsheet. D-502, H-512, M-503, T-512, S-505 and the remaining pumps/valves/exchangers were investigated in separate trial runs but are not in this converged run, so coverage will be incomplete.

D-501 is modelled as a truncated distillation column from the vapour draw down: 25 stages, feed_stage 2, Murphree efficiency 0.48, partial condenser at P_bar 2.026, vapor_mol_s 634, reflux_ratio 0.2 and bottoms_mol_s 5380. This follows the simulator guidance for a large vapour side draw rather than modelling the full 32-tray beer column with an explicit side draw.

Non-condensable CO2 is removed immediately upstream of D-501 by the auxiliary component_separator SEP-CO2 (Carbon dioxide recovery 0% to product, i.e. to S509G) because bubble-point column solvers stall on non-condensables; this is a fixed-split stand-in, not a design model of the actual overhead flash/vent.

Feed S506 in this run is set at 90 C and 2.026 bar with the data-sheet beer composition represented by DWSIM stand-ins (Water, Ethanol, Acetic acid, Glycerol, Carbon dioxide and glycol stand-ins for the lumped organics/solids) using the NRTL package; electrolyte/solids phase behaviour is not represented.

The small liquid distillate S509L from the partial condenser in this run (2423.6 kg/h in run trial-d501-2) is larger than the small overhead vent/condensate stream implied by the full Area 500 balance; the vapour product S510 is the calibrated stream. This split remains an open calibration gap.

No existing limits.* rating was raised. The submitted run spec contains no limits block; column diameter/tray-spacing limits used in the fuller trial runs (D-501 diameter_m 4.27, tray_spacing_m 0.61 from the P&ID 14 ft diameter and 24 in spacing) were not carried into this trial label.

H-512 in fuller trials was set with hot_out_T_C 47 C to match the interchanger cold-end condition, which conflicted with simultaneously matching the ~75-90 C beer feed temperature to D-501; that economizer/column heat-integration closure remains unresolved in the submitted run.

args.label: A500-full-v4
assumptions: All ten P&ID equipment items for Area 500 are present as units with their P&ID tags as unit ids in run A500-full-v4: H-512, D-501, T-512, D-502, H-503, M-503, H-506, H-507, H-509 and S-505. Auxiliary units SEP-CO2, MIX-509, MIX-523, MIX-524, MIX-512, SPLIT-514, REC-507 and REC-521 are routing/tear units only and are not claimed as P&ID equipment.

D-501 is modelled as a truncated distillation column from the vapour draw down (25 stages, feed_stage 2, Murphree efficiency 0.48, partial condenser, P_bar 2.026, vapor_mol_s 634, reflux_ratio 0.2, bottoms_mol_s 5380), following the simulator guidance for a large vapour side draw instead of the full 32-tray column with an explicit side draw. Its H-501 reboiler and H-504 condenser are the column-internal reboiler/condenser (reboiler_kW 64847.32, condenser_kW 15444.22 in run A500-full-v4), not separate hx units.

Non-condensable CO2 is removed immediately upstream of D-501 by auxiliary component_separator SEP-CO2 (Carbon dioxide recovery 0% to the column feed, reject S509G) because the bubble-point column solver stalls on non-condensables; this is a fixed-split stand-in, not a design model of the overhead vent system. The simulator additionally stripped 0.0363 kg/h of glycol/glycerol traces from D-502 feed S510 so that column converges.

The D-501 bottoms / H-512 feed-effluent loop and the molecular-sieve regeneration return to D-502 are closed with recycle tear units REC-507 (S507C -> S507) and REC-521 (S521C -> S521) because those loop temperatures are set by the column/sieve return mixing, per the task instruction. H-512 and H-506 are run in rating mode (U_W_m2K and installed area_m2 given, no hot_out_T_C over-specification); in the earlier trial A500-full-v3 imposing hot_out_T_C 47 on H-512 made the exchanger infeasible (64622 kW required vs 42385 kW available), so the 47 C value is retained only as the limits.out_T_C process requirement on the hot side and is reported as not met by the rating-mode outlet (S508 at 88.66 C) rather than by raising any rating.

D-502 is a rigorous distillation unit (45 stages, feed_stage [33, 14] for S510 and S521, efficiency 0.76, total condenser, P_bar 1.621, condenser_spec Reflux Ratio 3.5, reboiler_spec Boilup Ratio 3.0). Its simulated distillate S511L is 55.5 wt% ethanol, well below the near-azeotropic overhead the rectification section is intended to produce, and its Fair flood fraction is 1.072 against the 0.8 screen (utilisation 1.34 in run A500-full-v4); both are disclosed as unresolved calibration/limit findings of the as-built model, not adjusted away by changing documented geometry (diameter_m 3.96, tray_spacing_m 0.61) or limits.

M-503 (molecular sieve), T-512 (vent scrubber) and S-505 (solids filter/separator) are component_separator fixed-split stand-ins (M-503: Ethanol 99% / Water 1% recovered to the dry product; T-512: Ethanol and Acetic acid 99%, Water 50%, gases 0% to the scrubbed liquid; S-505: lumped-solids stand-ins HexaPropylene Glycol, PentaEthylene Glycol and TetraPropylene Glycol 100% to the cake stream S571, all other compounds 20%). These are not adsorption, absorption or solids-separation design models; the spec cannot express cyclic sieve adsorption/regeneration dynamics, scrubber mass transfer or filter cake washing, which remain model gaps rather than approximated physics.

The beer and bottoms lumped organics/solids are represented by the DWSIM stand-in compounds named in the operating data sheet (glycol/glycerol stand-ins for lignin, xylan, cellulose and soluble organics) with the NRTL package; electrolyte and solids phase equilibria are not represented. Feed compositions are mole fractions back-calculated so that the simulator reproduces the data-sheet component kg/h (verified on S501: Ethanol 21940.16 kg/h, Water 378524.26 kg/h in run A500-full-v4).

Utility and boundary streams S305, S317 (fermentation/saccharification vents to the scrubber) and S524 (scrubber water) enter as boundary feeds at the data-sheet flows (1969, 19180 and 26836 kg/h); the upstream areas that produce them are outside this unit's boundary. No existing limits.* rating has been raised: column limits use the P&ID geometry (D-501 diameter_m 4.27 from 14 ft and tray_spacing_m 0.61 from 24 in; D-502 diameter_m 3.96, tray_spacing_m 0.61) and H-512 limits use installed area_m2 310 with out_T_C 47 on the hot side.

args.label: A500-full-v5
assumptions: All ten P&ID equipment items for Area 500 are present as units with their P&ID tags as unit ids in run A500-full-v5: H-512, D-501, T-512, D-502, H-503, M-503, H-506, H-507, H-509 and S-505. Auxiliary units SEP-CO2, MIX-509, MIX-523, MIX-524, MIX-512, SPLIT-514, REC-507 and REC-521 are routing/tear units only and are not claimed as P&ID equipment.

D-501 is modelled as a truncated distillation column from the vapour draw down (25 stages, feed_stage 2, Murphree efficiency 0.48, partial condenser, P_bar 2.026, vapor_mol_s 634, reflux_ratio 0.2, bottoms_mol_s 5350, reduced from 5380 in run A500-full-v4), following the simulator guidance for a large vapour side draw instead of the full 32-tray column with an explicit side draw. Its H-501 reboiler and H-504 condenser are the column-internal reboiler (reboiler_kW 66425.66) and condenser (condenser_kW 16918.58) in run A500-full-v5, not separate hx units.

DISCLOSED SOLVER ERROR in run A500-full-v5: 'D-501: Failed to fulfill mass balance for Ethanol: Relative Error = 0.00014391734034284207 [Tolerance = 0.0001]'. Reducing bottoms_mol_s from 5380 (error 0.000256 in run A500-full-v4) to 5350 reduced but did not clear this tolerance failure; no documented limit was changed to mask it, and the D-501 product streams are nevertheless reported by the solver and calibrate closely to stream 510 (see calibration). This residual solver-tolerance closure is an open finding of the submitted run.

Non-condensable CO2 is removed immediately upstream of D-501 by auxiliary component_separator SEP-CO2 (Carbon dioxide recovery 0% to the column feed, reject S509G) because the bubble-point column solver stalls on non-condensables; this is a fixed-split stand-in, not a design model of the overhead vent system. The simulator additionally stripped 0.0341 kg/h of glycol/glycerol traces from D-502 feed S510 so that column converges (run A500-full-v5 notes).

The D-501 bottoms / H-512 feed-effluent loop and the molecular-sieve regeneration return to D-502 are closed with recycle tear units REC-507 (S507C -> S507) and REC-521 (S521C -> S521) because those loop temperatures are set by the column/sieve return, per the task instruction. H-512 and H-506 are run in rating mode (U_W_m2K and installed area_m2 given, no hot_out_T_C over-specification); in trial A500-full-v3 imposing hot_out_T_C 47 on H-512 made the exchanger infeasible (64622 kW required vs 42385 kW available), so the 47 C value is retained only as the limits.out_T_C process requirement on the hot side and is reported as not met by the rating-mode outlet (S508 at 87.67 C) rather than by raising any rating.

D-502 is a rigorous distillation unit (45 stages, feed_stage [33, 14] for S510 and S521, efficiency 0.76, total condenser, P_bar 1.621, condenser_spec Reflux Ratio 3.5, reboiler_spec Boilup Ratio 3.0). Its simulated distillate S511L carries Ethanol 26002.42 kg/h and Water 17990.78 kg/h, below the near-azeotropic overhead the rectification section is intended to produce, and its Fair flood fraction is 0.987 against the 0.8 screen (utilisation 1.234 in run A500-full-v5); both are disclosed as unresolved calibration/limit findings of the as-built model, not adjusted away by changing documented geometry (diameter_m 3.96, tray_spacing_m 0.61) or limits.

M-503 (molecular sieve), T-512 (vent scrubber) and S-505 (solids filter/separator) are component_separator fixed-split stand-ins (M-503: Ethanol 99% / Water 1% recovered to the dry product; T-512: Ethanol and Acetic acid 99%, Water 50%, gases 0% to the scrubbed liquid; S-505: lumped-solids stand-ins HexaPropylene Glycol, PentaEthylene Glycol and TetraPropylene Glycol 100% to the cake stream S571, all other compounds 20%). These are not adsorption, absorption or solids-separation design models; cyclic sieve adsorption/regeneration dynamics, scrubber mass transfer and filter cake washing are not expressible in the spec and remain model gaps rather than approximated physics.

The beer and bottoms lumped organics/solids are represented by the DWSIM stand-in compounds named in the operating data sheet (glycol/glycerol stand-ins for lignin, xylan, cellulose and soluble organics) with the NRTL package; electrolyte and solids phase equilibria are not represented. Feed compositions are mole fractions back-calculated so that the simulator reproduces the data-sheet component kg/h (verified on S501: Ethanol 21940.16 kg/h, Water 378524.26 kg/h in run A500-full-v5).

Utility and boundary streams S305, S317 (fermentation/saccharification vents to the scrubber) and S524 (scrubber water) enter as boundary feeds at the data-sheet flows (1969, 19180 and 26836 kg/h); the upstream areas that produce them are outside this unit's boundary. check_coverage on run A500-full-v4 reported no missing equipment; the connections it flagged as unmodelled are routed in the model through the auxiliary units named above (H-512 -> D-501 via SEP-CO2 on S506/S506L, D-501 -> H-512 via REC-507 on S507C/S507, D-501 -> T-512 via MIX-509/MIX-523/MIX-524, D-501 -> D-502 directly on S510, D-502 -> H-503 on S511L/S511, M-503 -> H-506 via SPLIT-514 on S514 and M-503 -> H-507 via MIX-512 on S512/S512M), i.e. they carry normal flow through renamed intermediate streams rather than being omitted.

No existing limits.* rating has been raised: column limits use the P&ID geometry (D-501 diameter_m 4.27 from 14 ft and tray_spacing_m 0.61 from 24 in; D-502 diameter_m 3.96, tray_spacing_m 0.61), H-512 limits use installed area_m2 310 with out_T_C 47 on the hot side, and H-506 limits use area_m2 100.
